t27 basics: the language in 27 lessons

Before the FPGA course: what a t27 spec is, how the compiler reads it, and what it gives back. Every lesson opens one table or diagram drawn from its own spec and one spec you can run in your browser.

Course 0, 27 lessons, one infographic and one t27 spec each: a module, constants and types, functions and tests, then the compiler's stages and the 7 languages it writes. It comes before the FPGA course.

All lessons

  • Module 1 · What a spec is

    A spec is one .t27 file: a module line, named values, and tests that check them.

  • Module 2 · The module line

    Every spec names its module once, with module, a name and a semicolon.

    1. 02 The module line

  • Module 3 · Comments and prose lines

    Two kinds of notes: a semicolon line of prose, and a comment after two slashes.

    1. 03 Comments and prose lines

  • Module 4 · Constants

    A constant gives a name, a type and a value, and the name never changes its value.

    1. 04 Constants

  • Module 5 · Whole numbers and their widths

    u8, u16, u32 and i32: how many bits a number has decides which values it can hold.

    1. 05 Whole numbers and their widths

  • Module 6 · True, false and text

    bool holds true or false; str holds text between double quotes.

    1. 06 True, false and text

  • Module 7 · Arrays

    An array has a length and a type, [5]u8, and its items are read by index from 0.

    1. 07 Arrays

  • Module 8 · Trits: minus one, zero, one

    A trit has three values, and three trits give 27 combinations.

    1. 08 Trits: minus one, zero, one

  • Module 9 · Expressions

    Arithmetic and comparison operators, and what a test can compute with them.

    1. 09 Expressions

  • Module 10 · A test block

    A test is a name and a list of asserts; each assert must be true.

    1. 10 A test block

  • Module 11 · Many tests in one spec

    Split checks into small named tests, so a failure points at one idea.

    1. 11 Many tests in one spec

  • Module 12 · Functions

    A function takes typed inputs and returns a typed result.

    1. 12 Functions

  • Module 13 · Local names: let and var

    Inside a function, let names a value once and var names one that changes.

    1. 13 Local names: let and var

  • Module 14 · Choices: if, else and switch

    if picks one of two paths; switch picks one of many by value.

    1. 14 Choices: if, else and switch

  • Module 15 · Loops: while and for

    while repeats while a condition holds; for walks a range of numbers.

    1. 15 Loops: while and for

  • Module 16 · pub or private

    pub marks a name for other modules; without it the name is the module's own.

    1. 16 pub or private

  • Module 17 · Structs

    A struct groups named fields, each with its own type.

    1. 17 Structs

  • Module 18 · Enums

    An enum names a fixed set of cases, and switch picks one of them.

    1. 18 Enums

  • Module 19 · Using other modules

    use names another module whose pub names this one may read.

    1. 19 Using other modules

  • Module 20 · Invariants and benches

    An invariant states a rule that must always hold; a bench names a measurement.

    1. 20 Invariants and benches

  • Module 21 · gen-ts: a spec becomes TypeScript

    gen-ts writes the constants of a spec as TypeScript, and leaves function bodies out.

    1. 21 gen-ts: a spec becomes TypeScript

  • Module 22 · Seven backends

    One spec, seven languages: what each backend of t27c writes.

    1. 22 Seven backends

  • Module 23 · The stages of t27c

    1. 23 The stages of t27c

  • Module 24 · tri: the command line

  • Module 25 · Reading compiler errors
